checks.why: an edit inside a lambda in a method body is a body change of THAT METHOD: the lambda is part of its body, and its one name, <lambda>, is never the declaration an edit is charged to (it matched every lambda in the graph, and their tests)
and what it reaches are the tests of that method, not the tests of every other lambda
control: an edit to the named method written next to the lambdas stays that method's
a lambda no method encloses (a table entry at the top level) is its own body change, named by where it is and targeted by file:line
its parameter list is read from the lambda's own header, never as a method signature
two lambdas in one method are two declarations: file:line names one of them, by its enclosing method and line
and the name printed for a lambda is a target that answers for that lambda alone
file:line on a module-level constant is that constant, not the body of the class above it
file:line on a class line is the class
control: file:line inside a method body is still that method, though the line assigns a field
